jessica (People Ops): Quick check — we're supporting a parent who's planning a phased return and wants to split their 12-week leave into two blocks + intermittent days. Does anyone have experience coordinating shift swaps and part-time coverage for this pattern? Trying to surface ops + paperwork needs.

matthew (eng): We did something similar last year. Main things: update oncall rotation, temporary redispatch of tickets, and clear handoff doc for the first 2 weeks.

sarah (frontend): @jessica is there an internal template for the handoff? I can volunteer to pair on the doc with the returning engineer.

emily (eng-manager): Also agree — set expectations about async turnaround, who owns critical alerts, and an explicit point of contact. We used a 2-week overlap shadow before and after leave for thehandoff.

jessica (People Ops): Thanks — yes there's a short checklist and a form the manager + employee must sign. HR portal link below (HR bot should post full form). For paperwork: signed leave request, medical certification if FMLA-eligible, and a phased-return agreement (dates + weekly hours). Deadline: submit at least 30 days before the planned start when possible.

hr-bot: Hi! Forms & guidance: https://redwood-internal.example/hr/leave-portal — required files: 1) Leave Request PDF, 2) Physician Certification, 3) Phased Return Agreement. Template handoff checklist: https://docs.google.com/example/parent-handoff-template. For urgent/last-minute requests, email people-ops@redwood.com. :white_check_mark:

sarah (frontend): quick Q — can the phased return be non-contiguous? e.g., 6 weeks on, 4 weeks off, then 6 weeks on? And does parental leave pay apply the whole time?

jessica (People Ops): Good Q. Policy excerpt: "Parental leave can be split into up to two separate blocks for bonding within the first 12 months; intermittent partial-day arrangements are considered and require manager approval." Pay: Redwood base parental pay covers the primary bonding period (up to 12 weeks). For intermittent days or additional blocks, pay may be prorated or use accrued PTO — we handle case-by-case. We'll escalate for a definitive payroll calc.

matthew (eng): Practically speaking, for coverage schedule, we used this approach: 1) calendar with blocked "do not schedule" windows, 2) designate 2 owners for the critical path, 3) reduce oncall frequency for the returning person for first 4 weeks.

emily (eng-manager): +1 on backup owners. Also add an item: update runbooks for the services they own. Sarah, if you can take the handoff template, I'll review and we can assign temporary owners.

sarah (frontend): I can start the template now. Quick snippet I'll put in the doc:```\nCritical endpoints: POST /checkout, /cart\nKnown flaky tests: cart-integration-spec\nHow to run locally: make dev && yarn test cart\nOncall playbook: runbook/cart-oncall.md\n```

jessica (People Ops): Perfect. I'll follow up with payroll about pay calculations and confirm whether the split you proposed fits policy. I'll drop the official intake form and a short ops checklist into the doc next. If anyone has questions about timing or want me to join a 15-min sync with the manager, ping me. :wave:
